validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, real, heavily documented FERC-jurisdictional project. FERC docket CP16-9(-000) approving Algonquin Gas Transmission, LLC and Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline, L.L.C.'s Atlantic Bridge expansion, approved Jan. 25-31, 2017 -- confirmed independently by RTO Insider (2017-01-30, headline + article:tag 'CP16-9'), Natural Gas Intel (2020-02-21, '132,700 Dth/d expansion... $452 million project... FERC granted Algonquin authorization... in January 2017'), Enbridge's own project page (docket 'CP16-9-000', 'Ownership: Algonquin Gas Transmission, LLC and Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline, L.L.C. (U.S.)'), and the U.S. EIA's official Natural Gas Pipeline Projects historical workbook (two line items: 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 1' operator Algonquin Gas Transmission, docket CP16-9, and 'Atlantic Bridge Project Phase 2'/'Phase 2 (CAN)'). This is not a GEM-only entity -- the sheet's own cited Kallanish, NGI, RTO Insider, Utility Dive, Enbridge, 2b1stConsulting, DeSmog and Boston Globe articles all independently corroborate it, and a live EIA government dataset row names it exactly. CLASSIFICATION: correctly Gas/transmission -- Algonquin Gas Transmission and Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline are FERC-regulated interstate transmission systems (EIA 'Pipeline Type: Interstate', 'Authority: FERC'), not gathering/gathering lines. DUPLICATE: checked against all 45 other rows in the roster -- no match; nothing else in the roster resembles this Northeast/Appalachian-sourced New England expansion. STATUS/CAPACITY/START confirmed for the Phase I segment specifically: EIA's 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 1' row states Operator=Algonquin Gas Transmission, Status=Completed, Completed Date=2017-11-01, Year In Service=2017, Beg_State=NJ, End_State=MA, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d)=40, Miles=0, Docket=CP16-9 -- this MATCHES the sheet's current Capacity=40.00 MMcf/d and StartYear1=2017 exactly. Independently, Enbridge's own project page states 'In November 2017, the first phase of Atlantic Bridge began service, providing 40,000 dekatherms per day of incremental firm transportation service' (40,000 Dth/d = 40 MMcf/d) and a Kallanish Energy trade-press piece (Feb. 2018, quoting Enbridge's own Erin Petkovich at a Marcellus-Utica Midstream conference) states 'The company's first phase of the Atlantic Bridge Pipeline began service last November and Phase 2 is scheduled to begin service in Q4 2018... will move an additional 40 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d)... The whole project, when completed, will move 135 MMcf/d.' Three independent sources (US government EIA data, Enbridge disclosure, independent trade press) agree on 40 MMcf/d for Phase I -- tier=high. StartYear2=2021 is also confirmed: Enbridge's project page states 'The Atlantic Bridge project was placed into full service in January 2021, following completion of the Weymouth Compressor Station' and EIA's Phase 2 / Phase 2 (CAN) rows both show Completed Date 2021-01-25 / Year In Service 2021 -- matches exactly. validity.recommendation: Change EndState/Province from 'Maine' to 'Massachusetts' for this row (the Phase I / Algonquin-only segment).
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's EndState/Province = 'Maine' is not supported by the two most authoritative sources on this specific segment. The U.S. EIA's official Natural Gas Pipeline Projects historical workbook splits Atlantic Bridge into three distinct project/operator line items: 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 1' (Algonquin Gas Transmission, Beg_State=NJ, End_State=MA, States='NJ,NY,CT,RI,MA' -- no ME), 'Atlantic Bridge Project Phase 2' (Algonquin, same NJ->MA states), and 'Atlantic Bridge Project Phase 2 (CAN)' (Maritimes & Northeast Pipeline, Beg_State=MA, End_State=NB [New Brunswick, Canada], States='MA, NH, ME, NB'). Maine only appears as a pass-through state on the SEPARATE Maritimes & Northeast Canadian-bound Phase 2(CAN) entry -- never as the End_State of any Algonquin-side entry, and the sheet's segment_name for this row is explicitly 'Phase I', which per EIA is entirely an Algonquin-system, NJ-to-MA project (Miles=0, capacity=40 MMcf/d, matching the sheet's own Capacity/StartYear1 exactly). Independently, Enbridge's own project overview page states: 'Project facilities in New York were placed into service in the fall of 2019, and allowed for the full project capacity to be available from New Jersey to Massachusetts' -- again naming Massachusetts, not Maine, as the U.S./Algonquin portion's terminus -- and separately describes Maine only as a downstream *market* served via the Weymouth compressor and the Maritimes & Northeast system ('facilitates delivery of much-needed natural gas to project customers in Maine and Atlantic Canada'), which is a different thing from the pipeline segment's own end state. Two independent sources (EIA government data + Enbridge's own disclosure) agree Massachusetts, not Maine, is the correct end state for the Algonquin/Phase I portion this row represents. Searched for a source that would put Maine as Phase I's specific end state and found none -- every source that gives a state-level endpoint for the Algonquin/'Phase I' side says Massachusetts.

Check whether a separate 'Phase II' PID exists elsewhere in the full GEM tracker outside this batch's 46-row roster -- if not, this may be an unrecorded gap (93 MMcf/d of capacity + the Canadian Maritimes & Northeast leg have no row at all).
validity.researcher_notes: The row currently mixes two different granularities: SegmentName='Phase I' and Capacity=40.00 MMcf/d are Phase-I-specific values (both confirmed against EIA + Enbridge + Kallanish, see the 'none' validity entry above), but StartYear2=2021 is Phase II's completion year, not Phase I's. Per EIA's historical workbook, 'Atlantic Bridge project Phase 1' (Algonquin, Completed Date 2017-11-01, Capacity 40 MMcf/d, Miles 0) and 'Atlantic Bridge Project Phase 2' (Algonquin, Completed Date 2021-01-25, Capacity 93 MMcf/d, Miles 6.3, Diameter 42in, Cost $451.8M) plus 'Atlantic Bridge Project Phase 2 (CAN)' (Maritimes & Northeast, Completed 2021-01-25, Capacity 93 MMcf/d) are THREE separate line items, not one. Enbridge's own project page corroborates: Phase I in service Nov. 2017 at 40,000 Dth/d, 'full service' only reached Jan. 2021 after the Weymouth compressor was finished. So a 'Phase I' row correctly carries Capacity=40/StartYear1=2017, but StartYear2=2021 belongs to a DIFFERENT phase with its own capacity (93 MMcf/d) that is not recorded anywhere on this row, nor (as far as this 46-row Appalachian/Mid-Atlantic roster shows) on any other row in scope -- the roster has no second Atlantic Bridge PID. This is a genuine spec/classification ambiguity, not a fabricated value, so I am not proposing a specific replacement StartYear2 -- the fix depends on a scope decision (split vs. merge) that should be made by whoever owns the row taxonomy, not inferred by this pass. I did NOT find a second, independent-of-Enbridge/EIA source that resolves this specific segment-vs-total ambiguity, since it is an artifact of how GEM structured the row, not a factual dispute between outside sources.
